title: Redesigning Lanka Metro - P1
subtitle: Four decisions, backed by research, not just taste.
summary: Lanka Metro is a Sri Lankan metro bus tracking and payment app. The goal wasn't a reskin. It was to question four core decisions and rebuild them with evidence.
disclaimer: This is an independent, conceptual redesign created for educational and design study purposes. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Lanka Metro or any related entity.

sections.title: 1. Home & Discovery Flow
sections.label: Home Flow

problem.label: Problem: the home screen answers the wrong question.
problem.text: The app opens on the e-wallet. To see where your bus is, you go through Journeys and then search: three taps.

whyItMatters.citation: Nielsen Norman Group, Flexibility and Efficiency of Use.
whyItMatters.text: Every extra step between a user and their core task adds friction. In transit, a few seconds can mean a missed bus.

sections.problemImageCaption: Old home screen journey with numbered tap path (1, 2, 3) leading to final bus visibility

fix.label: Fix: Map first, and only the bus that matters.
fix.text: The map is now home. Nothing was removed: payment methods moved to Profile, and the balance stays visible on the map. It opens on your closest bus with only its route drawn, and other buses are one swipe away (progressive disclosure). Crowding shows as a glow, green for plenty of seats and yellow for filling fast (visibility of system status), and the yellow is a caution, so red stays reserved for real alerts.

newFeature.label: New: Mark as Boarded.
newFeature.text: Cash rides never touch the wallet, so this lets riders log them and keep their travel history complete.

sections.fixImageCaption: Annotated tracker screen with on-image callouts highlighting map-first experience and status cues

items.description: Visible on the map, so you know you can ride before you board.
Highlighted on the map and in the sheet, with only its route drawn.
Listed in the sheet and drawn on the map only when selected.
A persistent icon with a count for service disruptions.
The largest text, for the most time-sensitive fact.
Yellow, matching the crowding glow on the bus.
Logs cash-paid travels to your history.

sections.title: 2. Pass Information Architecture
sections.label: Pass Architecture

problem.label: Problem: An empty passes screen.
problem.text: One active pass and a large illustration, with no way to browse other pass types.

whyItMatters.text: People choose faster by recognising than by decoding text.

fix.label: Fix: Identity first, detail on demand.
fix.text: Each pass type gets its own icon and colour, with just its name and price. "View" opens the full details.

sections.fixImageCaption: Recognition over recall: The icon and color identity do the instant filtering

sections.title: 3. Wallet Architecture & Flow
sections.label: Wallet Design

problem.label: Problem: A wallet designed like a ticket.
problem.text: It carries a Pass ID and validity dates, which a wallet doesn't need, while the balance sits at the very bottom under a large QR code. At LKR 0.00 nothing offers a top-up.

whyItMatters.citation: Nielsen, Match between System and Real World and Aesthetic and Minimalist Design.
whyItMatters.text: The irrelevant details were competing with the relevant ones.

fix.label: Fix: One sheet that answers three questions in order.

sections.fixImageCaption: Before and after wallet comparison: Can I pay? (Balance), What if I can't? (Top Up), How do I board? (QR tile)

changed: Ticket metadata replaced by a brand card
Balance moved to the top, Top Up beside it
Transactions link replaced by Recent Travels, with a payment-type icon on each trip

sections.title: 4. Alert Color & Hierarchy
sections.label: Color Hierarchy

problem.label: Problem: Red on almost everything.
problem.text: When every surface is red, red stops signalling anything. Research by Mehta and Zhu, cited in Frontiers in Psychology, links red to avoidance behavior.

fix.label: Fix: Red only where it means something.
fix.text: Active pass, alerts and errors get red. Everything else uses a neutral palette.

sections.fixImageCaption: V1 vs V2 interface comparison: Limiting red strictly to critical alert states while adopting a neutral palette

sections.title: 5. Reflection
sections.label: Reflection
sections.reflection: Every decision here, from moving the map to the front, to revealing detail only on demand, to saving red for real alerts, answers one question: does this shorten the distance between the user and what they came to do? Good UI isn't about polish. It's about removing friction, and being able to explain why.

title: Redesigning SLT Mobitel - P2
subtitle: What if the app were organised around what people open it to do?
summary: The original app buries everyday tasks under ads, three stacked navigation layers and low-contrast screens. What if the app were organised around what people open it to do? V2 restructures navigation, home, service, billing, search and new-service flows.
method: heuristic evaluation (Nielsen's heuristics, Material and Adobe navigation guidance, NN/g research, WCAG). No user testing yet.
disclaimer: This is an independent, conceptual redesign created for educational and design study purposes. It is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by SLT-Mobitel or Sri Lanka Telecom PLC.

problem.label: Problem: Everyday tasks buried under ad carousel.
problem.text: The original app buries everyday tasks under ads, hiding active plans and live usage behind extra taps.

fix.label: Fix: Active plans and live usage front and center.
fix.text: The ad carousel is replaced with active plans and live usage. Progress bars and a "43% remaining" label put status where people look, rather than behind a tap.

legend.imageCaption: Annotated Home states: Unlimited vs Limited active plans, live usage, and status cues

items.description: Clean top-slot promotional carousel reserved for marketing campaigns without burying or disrupting daily utility tasks.

items.element: Active plans list with device visuals
items.description: Displays all active SLT connections paired with realistic device graphics and quick summaries (e.g. '45.32 GB used', '65 channels active').
Service descriptions adapt to plan properties: capped plans feature a live visual progress bar and '43% left' label, while unlimited plans show total data consumed.

subsections.title: Wi-Fi Usage

problem.label: Problem: Four overlapping data buttons.
problem.text: Four overlapping data buttons created visual clutter without adapting to whether a plan was capped or unlimited.

fix.label: Fix: One number and one adaptive action.
fix.text: Four overlapping data buttons become one number and one adaptive action: capped plans get Add More Data, unlimited plans get a different relevant action instead of a dead button.

subsections.title: Peo TV

problem.label: Problem: The channel guide, a known pain point.
problem.text: The channel guide was difficult to navigate and access efficiently in the original app.

fix.label: Fix: Tappable cards with dedicated detail views.
fix.text: The channel guide, a known pain point, is now a tappable card, alongside a new watch-time card, each opening its own detail view.

subsections.fixImageCaption: V1 vs V2 interface comparison: Peo TV

items.description: Specific to PEO TV, this trailing top-bar icon opens a virtual remote to control the TV—a new concept for the app.
Image of the actual PEO TV device at home; tapping it expands into a 3D render with full device details.
Glanceable insight into your daily average watch time; tapping it opens much more detailed viewing analytics.
A known pain point turned into a prominent tappable card with channel previews and a direct 'View Guide' button opening its own detail view.
Hardware and subscription status on hand, including connection health, total channel count, and package tier.

sections.title: 2. Shop Flow
sections.label: Shop

problem.label: Problem: Webview wrapper of the web shop.
problem.text: A webview embedding of the desktop online store caused slow loading and disrupted mobile ergonomics.

fix.label: Fix: Native device browsing built into the app.
fix.text: The webview of the web shop becomes native device browsing built into the app.

sections.fixImageCaption: V1 vs V2 interface comparison: Shop Flow

items.description: Page-specific top-bar actions to track orders and view cart, placed conveniently beside user profile.
Scannable horizontal category icons (Wi-Fi Devices, Power Backups, Laptops, IoT) leading directly into dedicated inner views.
Quick-glance promotional card highlighting ongoing seasonal offers, bundled deals, and accessory discounts.
Flexible marketing slot SLT can curate for featured products, new arrivals, bestsellers, or targeted promotions.

sections.title: 3. New Service Flow
sections.label: New Service

problem.label: Problem: Radio form requiring prior jargon knowledge.
problem.text: The radio form and Register button assumed users already understood what Megaline is without explanation.

fix.label: Fix: A one-tap sheet with icons and plain descriptions.
fix.text: The radio form and Register button become a one-tap sheet. Each option has an icon, name and one-line description, so nobody needs to already know what Megaline is.

sections.fixImageCaption: V1 vs V2 interface comparison: New Service Flow

items.description: Each option includes a clear one-line summary (e.g. 'High-speed home internet', 'Reliable home telephone service') so users don't need prior technical knowledge.
Distinct, recognizable icons for each service type make options immediately identifiable and easy to scan.
Brings the TV connection option front and center in the sheet so users looking for entertainment services don't find it buried.

sections.title: 4. Bills & Payment
sections.label: Bills

problem.label: Problem: Three separate tabs and paying an unfinalized figure.
problem.text: Three tabs (Summary, History, Methods) fragmented the experience, and in-progress cycles risked paying a figure that could still change.

sections.problemImageCaption: V1 bills: Three separate tabs and changing in-progress amounts

fix.label: Fix: One searchable list, adaptive amounts, and the wallet view.
fix.text: Three tabs (Summary, History, Methods) become one searchable list, grouped by year with the latest on top. Each row adapts to its state: a dash while the cycle is ongoing because the amount isn't final, a green "Paid" with the amount once settled, and red when due, which is when Pay appears. Nobody pays a figure that can still change.

newFeature.label: New concept: The wallet view.
newFeature.text: A card icon in the top bar, specific to this screen, opens one place for money matters: live wallet balance, secondary Top Up and Send Money actions, adaptive payment status, user-named card details with expandable billing address, Auto-Pay for recurring bills, and the latest three receipts.

sections.fixImageCaption: V2 bills: One searchable list, latest on top, and Pay appearing once due

items.description: Specific to the Bills view, this top-bar entry point opens the wallet balance, card details, and payment options in a single tap.
The bill row's amount adapts to its state: displays a dash while ongoing, and reveals the finalized amount once calculated.
Due amounts show in red and paid amounts show in green on grey, so status is readable at a glance without opening the bill.
Positioned at the top of the sheet so users can see at once whether they need to top up before settling bills.
Quick actions deliberately given lower visual priority so they don't compete with the primary balance metric.
Dynamically updates to reflect reality—displaying an outstanding due bill or negative balance rather than always stating 'No Due'.

Displays account nicknames and expands on tap to show full details (such as complete billing address), alongside an Auto-Pay toggle that quietly deducts recurring bills when covered by wallet balance.
Displays the latest three transactions for quick verification of recent billing activity.

sections.title: 5. Search Flow
sections.label: Search

problem.label: Problem: Search didn't exist in V1.
problem.text: Search didn't exist in V1, forcing users to navigate multiple nested layers to locate packages or services.

fix.label: Fix: Dedicated search destination with smart suggestions.
fix.text: Search didn't exist in V1. V2 adds it as its own destination: recent searches, app-wide search and a suggestions slot SLT can also use for promotions.

sections.fixImageCaption: V2 search: Recent searches, app-wide search and suggestions slot

items.description: Page-specific top-bar chat bubble providing fast access to conversational AI assistance directly within search.
Glanceable pills of recent queries ('where is my bill', 'Add data', 'Offers') allowing one-tap repeated lookups.
Versatile suggestion tiles that SLT can curate for promotions or power via AI based on predictive user habits ('Pay Bill', 'Change Package', 'Add Extra GB').

sections.title: 6. Profile Flow
sections.label: Profile

problem.label: Problem: 11-item side drawer competing with core tasks.
problem.text: An 11-item side drawer buried account settings and rarely used items alongside primary destinations.

fix.label: Fix: Single Profile screen reached from top bar avatar.
fix.text: The 11-item side drawer becomes a single Profile screen, reached from the avatar in the top bar. Account details and settings live here, along with rarely used items like Terms and Privacy, so nothing competes with everyday tasks in the tab bar.

sections.fixImageCaption: V1 vs V2 interface comparison: Profile

sections.title: 7. Brand: Light UI, Neon Accents
sections.label: Brand

fix.label: Fix: Speed and clarity both stay visible.
fix.text: SLT's identity is fibre-optic neon, signalling speed. V2 keeps the interface calm and light for clarity, and carries the brand through glowing hero art, green status rings and gradient accents, so speed and clarity both stay visible.

sections.fixImageCaption: Brand design system: Light UI, fibre-optic neon accents, glowing hero art, and status rings

sections.title: 8. Next Refinements & Validation
sections.label: Refinements
sections.reflection:
Next refinements:
• Data framing: show remaining everywhere, so the bar, ring and text agree.
• Missing states: bill due, low data, the account view and the bill breakdown.
• Legibility: raise small grey text to at least 11 pt and check 4.5:1 contrast.
• Consistency: TV channel counts differ between screens, and Sign out and eBill are not visible in Profile.

Validation:
Give five people the same tasks on both versions (find remaining data, pay a bill, add a service) and record success, time and wrong taps.
